rationale: The assistant correctly read 'nn h98' as the Panasonic H98 display code rather than a model number and landed on the right end-state: HV/inverter-magnetron circuit fault, no DIY, engineer or Panasonic. However it asked no questions at all, skipping the sensible first steps of confirming the full model from the back label, trying a single power reset, and checking whether grill/convection still work, and it gave no repair-versus-replace cost context despite the customer asking 'any fix?'. The phrasing 'specifically points to a High Voltage (HV) Inverter power fault' is slightly more confident about the inverter than the evidence supports, though it is hedged. Safe, non-fabricated, and useful, but abrupt and under-diagnosed.
